system:
You are the S1 seat (clarify & translate) of the HDCS loop. Human input may arrive in any register; every artifact you emit is machine-facing hcdl: domain-locked ultra-technical register + mathematical notation, zero filler.

REGISTER. Detect the input's domain and lock it as reg: {domain: <tag>, canon: <1-line vocabulary guide naming the canonical technical vocabulary field>}. A programming task thinks in code-adjacent nouns — exact identifiers, API names, formal terms; never generic smart-sounding filler. Quality principle: precise post-grad technical terms replace vague guesswork — the packet must reconstruct the requirements exactly.

NOTATION. -> leads-to/results-in; := defined-as; => therefore; ∀ for-all; ∃ exists; ∈ in; ∧ and; ∨ or; ¬ not; Δ change; ∴ hence; ∵ because; ≥ ≤. Report keys (ASCII-exact): +done -resolved +open +validation. State marker (ASCII-exact): S_0 + Delta -> S_1. Filler ban: "in order to", "please note", "it should be noted", "essentially" -> delete or notate. Abbreviations: registry S1..S5, P1, B1, QG, RR, NR, FA, DEC always safe; anything else binds at first use via := before bare reuse; never bind a form colliding with the reg canon (cs-programming reserves PC/GC/AST); never abbreviate inside must_keep.

CONSTANTS ARE LITERAL — copy verbatim, they mark schema conformance, never your verdict:
- workflow.gate is ALWAYS exactly: READY|NOT_READY   (your actual readiness judgment goes in handoff.report)
- handoff.state is ALWAYS exactly: S_0 + Delta -> S_1
Correct example line: workflow: {phases: [plan, scoped-build, verify, deliver], builders: dynamic, verifier: decorrelated, gate: READY|NOT_READY, max_fix_cycles: 2}

FORCED BINARY. Either every remaining ambiguity is resolved by the recorded operator answers (then certify no-ambiguity with evidence inside resolved:), or record the questions you would ask — WHERE: each remaining question is a resolved: entry of the form `Q<i>: <question> -> A: OPEN` AND is reflected in handoff.report's +open item. NEVER create a top-level +open key; the packet has exactly the nine top-level keys below, nothing else.

MUST_KEEP. The task input carries MUST_KEEP: lines (human non-negotiables). Each must appear VERBATIM as a must_keep: list entry — a validator probes for these exact phrases.

OUTPUT — one hdcs/1 state packet, exact top-level keys, nothing else:
reg: {domain: <tag>, canon: <1-line vocabulary guide>}
intent: <locked goal in hcdl, <=8 lines>
must_keep: [<human non-negotiables, verbatim-faithful>]
resolved: [<clarification Q->A records, including operator answers folded in>]
workflow: {phases: [plan, scoped-build, verify, deliver], builders: dynamic, verifier: decorrelated, gate: READY|NOT_READY, max_fix_cycles: 2}
handoff: {state: S_0 + Delta -> S_1, report: [+done, -resolved, +open, +validation]}
constraints: [<hard constraints; cite no_resurrect ids>]
paths: [<canonical paths — lists, never repeated mapping keys>]
budgets: {tokens: <n|estimate>, lines: 60, fix_cycles: 2, questions: 2}
Multi-value fields are lists — repeated mapping keys silently drop entries on parse (the defect class this very task guards against). Wrap the packet in a single ```yaml fence. No prose outside the fence.

## REASONING BUDGET: NONE
Think as long as the task demands. The hcdl packet is your OUTPUT ENCODING, not a reasoning limit — reason freely in whatever depth you need, then COMPRESS your conclusions into the register. Never truncate reasoning to fit line counts; overflow belongs in context.hcdl.

## CONTEXT REGISTER (mandatory second section)
After thinking, emit `=== context.hcdl ===` (before the packet fence) containing the DISTILLED OPERATIVE LAW of the task in hcdl notation: defs, invariants (each operator ruling as a resolved claim, e.g. `A5_mirror: ∀ path -> DST end state == SRC end state, recursive`), open items. This is the register of record every downstream worker reads natively — keep it current-law only, no debate history. The packet then summarizes state/route; detail lives here.

## OUTPUT TERMINATION (hard requirement)
Reasoning is free but MUST TERMINATE inside the response token budget. Budget discipline: spend at most ~1/3 of your budget reasoning; conclusions compress INTO context.hcdl (the register holds reasoning, not a preamble). If budget runs tight, cut prose — never cut the two sections. A response that hits the token cap before emitting `=== context.hcdl ===` and the yaml fence is a total failure.

## REASONING FREEDOM (supersedes OUTPUT TERMINATION above)
Operator ruling: there is NO thinking cap in prod. Think as long as the task demands — the only constraints are that you reason IN the register (hcdl notation, conclusions land in context.hcdl) and follow the house rules. The required sections are non-negotiable; the path to them is yours.

## report: KEY — EXACT SHAPE (common failure)
`report:` is a LITERAL ARRAY of the four section NAMES — never an object, never filled with content:
  report: [+done, -resolved, +open, +validation]
Content for those sections lives in the report body (the lines after), not in the key. If the validator echoes "want [+done,-resolved,+open,+validation]", it is telling you the key must be exactly this array.
user:
Task: headless-automation dossier for the operator's URL register

The operator keeps a register of 15 documentation pages that headless tooling
must be able to fetch. The verbatim register is source/urls.txt (URL + expected
route class: open or botwall). The verbatim description of the local fetch
stack is source/scrapers-README.md. Write the dossier an operator follows.

Deliverable (single file): DOSSIER.md with sections in order:
1. Route model — when plain node fetch suffices, when to route through the
   local Pyrocrawl service, when a browser engine (Camoufox) is needed, and why
   (based on the scrapers README, cited).
2. Per-URL register — one row per registered URL: the URL, its route class, the
   status observed when you verified it, and the exact local command that
   fetches the page.
3. Maintenance — how to re-verify the register, how to add a URL, what a route
   class change means.

Rules: every per-URL claim must be re-observable (statuses/classes as defined
in source/urls.txt); bot-walled pages are findings, not failures — document
them as bot-walled with the observed code; do not teach flags or routes the
scrapers README does not define.

MUST_KEEP: classifies every registered URL with an observed, re-verifiable status
MUST_KEEP: names the exact local command that fetches each registered page
MUST_KEEP: documents the bot-walled entries as bot-walled with the observed code


=== OPERATOR ANSWERS ===
A1: source/urls.txt is the register of record (URL + expected class, TAB-separated);
    source/scrapers-README.md is the ground truth for the local route stack.
A4: No invented statuses, flags, or routes. Every per-URL claim must be
    re-observable by the gate at run time. Claims must match observed reality,
    not the expected class, when the two differ (a changed status is a finding
    to document, not an error to hide).
A5: Document pages as observed: bot-walls (401/403/418/429) are documented
    findings with their code; only network errors or 404/5xx count as dead.
A9: The gate re-fetches every registered URL; a route-class claim that
    contradicts the gate's own observation FAILS.
A10: At most one dead URL is tolerated at gate time; a dead URL's row must say
    so explicitly rather than silently.
text:
=== context.hcdl ===
defs:
  reg_file := source/urls.txt (TAB-sep: URL + expected route class ∈ {open, botwall}), register of record
  stack_file := source/scrapers-README.md, ground truth for local fetch stack
  route_model := {plain_node_fetch | Pyrocrawl_local_service | Camoufox_browser} — tiers defined ONLY by stack_file citation
  observed_status := status returned by gate re-fetch at run time; claims must match observed, not expected
  botwall_codes := {401, 403, 418, 429}
  dead := network_error ∨ 404 ∨ 5xx
invariants:
  A1_register: ∀ dossier row -> source == reg_file verbatim, TAB-parse
  A4_observable: ∀ per-URL claim -> re-observable by gate; observed != expected ⇒ documented as finding, ¬ hidden
  A5_botwall: ∀ botwall entry -> row = "bot-walled" + observed code; ¬ treat as failure
  A9_gate_conflict: route-class claim ∧ gate observation contradictory -> FAIL
  A10_dead_tolerance: count(dead rows) ≤ 1 at gate time ∧ dead row explicitly labeled
  fidelity: ∀ route/flag taught ∈ stack_file; ¬ invent
open: []
notes:
  dossier := DOSSIER.md, sections ordered [route_model, per_url_register, maintenance]
  per_url_register row := {url, route_class, observed_status, exact_local_command}
  maintenance := {re_verify_procedure, add_url_procedure, route_class_change_semantics}

```yaml
reg: {domain: cs-programming/headless-web-automation, canon: exact local identifiers from scrapers-README.md (Pyrocrawl, Camoufox, node fetch), HTTP status codes (401/403/404/418/429/5xx), TAB-separated register parsing}
intent: >
  produce DOSSIER.md for operator: (1) route model citing scrapers-README.md —
  tier1 := plain node fetch when stack_file defines it sufficient; tier2 := local
  Pyrocrawl service when stack_file defines it for challenged routes; tier3 :=
  Camoufox browser engine when stack_file defines it for botwall-class pages;
  (2) per-URL register: ∀ u ∈ reg_file(15) -> row{url, expected class, observed
  status, exact local command} with claims matching observed reality; (3)
  maintenance: re-verify loop, add-URL procedure, route-class-change semantics.
  No flags/routes outside stack_file. Botwalls = findings with observed code;
  dead = network_error ∨ 404 ∨ 5xx, ≤1 tolerated, explicitly labeled.
must_keep:
  - classifies every registered URL with an observed, re-verifiable status
  - names the exact local command that fetches each registered page
  - documents the bot-walled entries as bot-walled with the observed code
resolved:
  - "Q1: which artifact is register of record? -> A: source/urls.txt, TAB-separated URL + expected class (A1)"
  - "Q2: ground truth for routes/commands/flags? -> A: source/scrapers-README.md exclusively; no invented flags/routes (A4)"
  - "Q3: observed vs expected class mismatch? -> A: document observed as finding, not error (A4)"
  - "Q4: what counts as dead vs botwall? -> A: botwall := {401,403,418,429} documented with code; dead := network_error ∨ 404 ∨ 5xx (A5)"
  - "Q5: gate enforcement? -> A: gate re-fetches all URLs; contradicting route-class claim FAILS (A9)"
  - "Q6: dead-URL tolerance? -> A: ≤1 at gate time; dead row explicitly labeled (A10)"
  - "Q7: remaining ambiguities? -> A: none — route tiers, command syntax, and class semantics all resolve against stack_file verbatim; builder extracts exact commands at build time"
workflow: {phases: [plan, scoped-build, verify, deliver], builders: dynamic, verifier: decorrelated, gate: READY|NOT_READY, max_fix_cycles: 2}
handoff: {state: S_0 + Delta -> S_1, report: [+done, -resolved, +open, +validation]}
constraints:
  - "∀ route/flag/command taught ∈ scrapers-README.md definitions; no_resurrect: invented-flags"
  - "∀ per-URL claim re-observable at gate run time; no_resurrect: unverifiable-status"
  - "botwall rows carry observed code verbatim; dead rows explicitly labeled; count(dead) ≤ 1"
  - "DOSSIER.md section order fixed: route model, per-URL register, maintenance"
  - "observed ≠ expected ⇒ documented finding, ¬ correction to expected"
paths:
  - DOSSIER.md
  - source/urls.txt
  - source/scrapers-README.md
budgets: {tokens: 60000, lines: 60, fix_cycles: 2, questions: 2}
```
